#### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When running tests for the dynamic ressource allocation manager, a fake gRPC server is setup and in some cases a timeout greater than the default client timeout is used to ensure that when preparing/unpreparing ressources take longer than the default timeout an error is correctly raised.
A fix has already been merged aiming to fix #121710. However when the CI is doing some heavy lifting the additional 30ms used to test the timeout isn't enough as reported [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121774#issuecomment-1886259309).

review_comments:
@TommyStarK Thank you for the PR! 
Just wondering if we can increase plugin.PluginClientTimeout instead of this. Can you remind me what was an initial purpose of using hardcoded addition?

I can't recall that we have consensus that hardcoded this. we were first setup a wrong testcase then @TommyStarK  address the wrong test case and start using this hardcoded to setup fake grpc server. That's all I can get in my mind
If I recall correctly Kevin increased the hardcoded value because he experienced some timeouts. Here is the link towards his comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117146

I'm still not sure I fully understand the purpose of additional hardcoded value. Is this something specific to the test? Where the delay comes from when the test is run in CI? If grpc calls take more time then we should increase `plugin.PluginClientTimeout`.
me either, let's wait @klueska for having a better understanding

this is trying to make the server take *just* over the length of time the client will wait before timing out, to *trigger* the client observing a timeout. However, the client timeout is triggered via a context with a deadline, which is not guaranteed to cancel at *precisely* the deadline... in a busy CI env the context cancel might happen quite a bit later than the deadline.

Timeout coordination at the millisecond level is not reliable in often-underresourced CI environments.

Expanding this to a second to make sure the server delays long enough for the client to have a better chance at experiencing the timeout is a good short-term fix to stabilize this test (this is also flaking in 1.29 and 1.28 release branch runs and should be picked back).
